Understanding how to set your carriage for PLAIN KNITTING is essential
It is a good habit to always check your carriage settings before starting a new technique or a new piece of knitting. It's easy to have your carriage set for patterning, then come back days later and be surprised that the machine isn't knitting as expected.
Every time you sit down to knit, take time to double check the settings.

1. Cam Lever
2. Stitch Dial 5
3. Russel Lever(s)
4. Weaving Knob(s) (up)
5. Yarn Feeder

Save your back, neck and shoulders
In the videos in this course, you'll see me pushing the carriage with one hand. BAD!!!! I'm reaching around the camera.
When you are knitting use both hands and push and pull alternately to move the carriage.
Many knitters also adjust their knitting table so they can stand while knitting.

Arm, hand and wrist position

STOP! LOOK AT THE POSITION OF YOUR HAND AND WRIST IN RELATION TO YOUR ELBOW. Many knitters will find their elbow is below the level of the wrist and hand.
Knitting in this position, after a time, will create an ache and pain through the neck and across the shoulders. Try sitting higher so that your elbow is slightly above the wrist and hand.

More tips

  • A stool for your feet may be needed or your machine table or stand may have to be lowered.
  • If you have a stand to use your machine, the same elbow position is needed. (elbows slightly above the hands)
  • Try standing to knit. Use an adjustable table to keep the elbow position correct.
  • Good lighting is a must
  • A clean (and oiled) machine bed and carriage are essential.

This machines uses external devices for automatic patterning. (Unlike Brother/Knit-King machines with built-in electronics)
This course focuses on how to use DesignaKnit to talk to the machine and choose the right needles for stitch patterns.

REQUIRED:

  1. 1 PC and DesignaKnit
  2. 2 SilverLink 4 or 5 box
  3. 3 USB cable (from PC to SilverLink Box)
  4. 4 Curl Cord (from SilverLink Box to Carriage)
  5. 5 Power cord for SilverLink Box

NOTE: The N-1 Cam (Needle 1) is NOT used with DesignaKnit

Connect the electronics

  • Connect the PC to the SilverLink Box with the USB cable.
  • Connect power to the SilverLink Box with the power cord.
  • Position the Curl Cord on the tension mast (cable toward you).
  • Connect the Curl Cord to the carriage.

Don't try to bend (or "repair) a bent needle .. replace it!
Heaven forbid that you bend a needle (it happens).
Replacing it shouldn't be a problem. Keep spare needles on hand.
If you don't have a spare needle, you can "borrow" a needle from the end of the needlbed tempororarily

On Silver Reed machines, point cams determine the range of pattern knitting. They slide along the back of the needle bed, and pattern knitting occurs only between the two point cams.

Place the point cams at both edges of the knitting to work the pattern across the entire row. For an isolated motif, position one point cam on each side of the desired motif area. The needles outside the point cams will continue knitting in plain stockinette.

Point cams are used with the Needle 1 Cam. See page 19 of the Silver Reed 840 Operation Manual for additional information.

View Point Cams in the Knitting Glossary

Whether aligned by electronics or manually positioned, the needle position along with the carriage settings create stitch patterns.
Vintage machine knitting patterns and instructions will refer often to these positions with abbreviations.
A Non-working position  (NWP)  Unused needles
B  Working Position (WP)  Needles lined up to knit in stockinette and most pattern work
C  Middle Position (MP)  Bring the needles from holding position into working and pattern work positions
D  Holding Position (HP/Hold)  The farthest position from "A" on the needlebed

Open Cast on
By definition, an open cast on will have stitches that will unravel if given the chance.
Some machine manuals will give instruction for this type of cast on
The Cast on demonstrated in the previous video is an open cast on.
Here are some variations:
  • Open Cast on with a cast on Comb (shown in the video)
  • Open Cast on with a wire
  • Open Cast on with Ravel cord
Most knitters graduate beyond these methods pretty quickly.
The following cast on methods leave open stitches to be worked later. For example, leave open stitches, then pick them up and hand knit some ribbing. Or turn the knitting, pick up open stitches and knit reverse stockinette.
  • Scrap and Ravel
  • Using a Cast on Rag
You will use these again and again

Closed Cast on
With a closed cast on, the starting stitches are secure.
These techniques can be categorized:
  • Closed but temporary.
    These cast on methods are quick and have their place ... they just wouldn't be appropriate for the finished edge of your next sweater.
    Uses:
    • Cast on for swatching
    • Scrap 'n Ravel Cast on
    • Cut 'n Sew
  • Closed and Functional
    These techniques can be used for the edges of your knitting, without any additional finishing.
    • E-wrap cast on (lots of variations)
    • Chain Cast on

When you are just getting started exploring your machine, the number of stitches to cast on and rows to knit isn't critical. Measuring over 40 stitches and 60 rows is the recommended standard for your machine. This standard was established by using a Gauge Ruler to measure gauge.

No matter how you measure, establishing gauge IS CRITICAL to success with your knitting machine.

To knit a "proper" swatch (in any stitch pattern)

  1. Cast on 60 stitches with the method of your choice
  2. Knit 10 rows with your garment yarn
  3. Knit 2 rows with a contrasting color (similar weight yarn)
  4. Knit 20 rows. Isolate and mark 40 stitches (needles L21 and R21)
  5. Knit 20 rows. Isolate and mark 40 stitches
  6. Knit 20 rows. (a total of 60 rows after the contrasting row)
  7. Knit 2 rows with a contrasting color
  8. Knit 10 rows with the garment yarn
  9. Bind off (this is a good time to practice different bind off methods)

blocks.title: About Automatic Patterning on this Machine

components.html:
Don't Skip This!

You can carefully slide your carriage off the needlebed to examine the underside.
There's no mystery or magic to how the carriage works!
The needle butts are directed through channels. Depending on each needle position and your carriage settings, the needles will either pick up yarn and knit or not (forming stitch patterns).
Don't be overwhelmed by this geeky stuff ... just follow along to get a general idea of how things work.

DesignaKnit can be used in three different ways, depending on whether you are making an all-over stitch pattern, placing a motif, or knitting a shaped garment with a stitch pattern.

  1. Knit a Stitch Pattern — for swatches, rectangles, and knitting with an all-over stitch pattern.
  2. Position a Stitch Pattern — for isolated motifs, borders, and custom placement on the knitting.
  3. Knit a Garment in Pattern — for knitting a shaped garment piece while using a stitch pattern.

components.html:
Here are 4 accessories that are needed for automatic patterning.
We will discuss them in detail in the associated techniques sections.

Yarn Separators

If your yarn tangles with the round brushes under the carriage, try using the Yarn Separators on each side. This is especially recommended when knitting Fairisle.

Point Cams

Pattern knitting only happens between 2 point cams.
  • When setting Point cams at both edges of the knitting, the pattern will be knitted across the entire row. Needles outside of the point cams will not pattern.
  • When knitting isolated motif, position the point cam on each side of where you want the motif to knit, keeping the other sections in plain knitting.

No sound

Needle-1 Cam

The needle-1 (N-1) cams are NOT used with DesignaKnit
  • The red line of the Needle-1 cam tells the machine where to start and finish the pattern repeat.
  • Usually, the Needle-1 Cam is put at the center of the needlebed.
  • NOTE: The Needle-1 Cam MUST be placed within the 2 point cams or at either Point Cam. Do not put it outside the Point Cams

sections.title: The importance of End needle Selection
sections.bodyHtml:
For easier seaming and neater edges, prevent the end needles from patterning.
Having a tuck or slip stitch on the edge of the knitting distorts the edge.
Use this one little trick for neat edges.

sections.title: End needle Selection on this machine
sections.bodyHtml:
To prevent the end needles from patterning on this machine, move the Point cams 1-2 stitches from the edge of the knitting.

PLUS . . . .

Many stitch patterns recommend pulling the end needle next to the carriage all the way out to deal with the end needles. See each stitch technique description.

As you are knitting in pattern, you may receive this message:


This indicates that the SENSOR didn't pass the magnet on the needlebed.

How to fix?

Short rows, Partial Knitting, Hold Setting all involve preventing selected needles from knitting.
Often referred to as the Hold Setting. On this machine partial knitting is accomplished with the Russel Levers.

Tuck is a great way
to add texture and interest to your knitting.
When knitting tuck, certain needles do not knit and the working yarn travels OVER the needles out of work.
Very often Tuck stitch is used as a wrong-side facing stitch pattern. The texture of the tucks combined with the purl side of the knitting is very pleasing. But often the knit side can be even more appealing.
Once you understand how tuck stitch is created on your machine, the sky's the limit!
  • The general rule: no 2 tuck stitches next to each other
  • Tuck limitations: - 3-4 adjacent tuck rows are best (depending on your yarn) - the stitches "build up" on the needles, so less is best
  • In DesignaKnit use the Tuck symbols:
    • Let DAK apply any tuck rules for an accurate stitch pattern
    • Send the correct information to the machine to create tuck stitch


For more about Tuck, visit:
the Knit it Now Classroom: Tuck Talk
Tuck Stitch Examples
Check out the Knit it Now Stitch Library for Tuck and Tuck lace Inspiration! Here are a few samples:

Knit a swatch 60 stitches by 100 rows in 1x1 tuck
1x1 tuck: Notice every other needle tucks (yarn over the needle) every other row

Checklist:
Connect computer, Silverlink, Curl Cord and machine
In Interactive Knitting, set up the swatch size
Set the point cams to the edges of the knitting
Set the cam lever to TUCK
Follow the Interactive Knitting Prompts

Unlike Fairisle, Multi-color tuck is worked by swapping out yarn colors either manually or with a color changer.

This is an example of a beautiful right-side facing tuck stitch
3 color tuck.stp

Multi-color Tuck Challenge

  1. Download the 3 color tuck stitch pattern
  2. Set up and knit the stitch pattern in 1 color
  3. Observe how the stitches and the "bumps" form with the 4 rows of tuck
  4. Manually change colors as directed by Interactive Knitting and watch the magical color changes
  5. If you have a color changer now may be a good time to set it up and learn to use it

Tuck Lace creates a beautiful lace-like fabric without a lace carriage or stitch transfers.
Master tuck stitch and put needles out of work to create tuck lace. This technique can be worked on both the single and double bed.

Tuck Lace on the SK840

The hardest part of knitting tuck lace is determining which needles should be out of work.
Here's a TIP:

You just ripped out a row of knitting or you put some knitting back on the bed from the garter bar or you did a bit of shaping and now your carriage is on the opposite side of the working yarn.
Free pass is a method of moving the carriage across the knitting without knitting or dropping stitches.
Positioning the carriage is an essential skill for machine knitters.
Here are 4 ways to "free pass" to get the carriage to the same side as the working yarn without knitting or dropping stitches.

1Remove the carriage

Sure, you could take the carriage off the machine, run to the other end and replace the carriage ... but that's a "rookie move". Take control of your machine and use the carriage settings.

2Use the hold setting

2 steps:
  1. Put all needles in hold position
  2. Set the carriage to hold (engage the Russel Levers )
When you pass the carriage, the needles will not move and stitches will not drop or knit.

3"Pop" the carriage (Silver Reed/ Singer/Studio machines)

Pop the carriage (silver machines). Use the Carriage Release and raise the top section of the carriage.
The carriage will pass across without knitting or dropping stitches.

4Hold the Side lever


With all needles in "B" Position, hold the side lever and pass the carriage in that direction (continue to hold the lever across the row) No needles will knit or drop.

Don't forget to reset your row counter after a free pass.

Take time to practice Free Pass

It is so important that you know how to move your carriage without knitting or dropping stitches, it is worth the time to cast on a few stitches, knit a few rows and practice all 4 free pass methods:
  1. Remove the carriage and move it to the opposite side of the bed

  2. Put all needles in hold ("D") and use the hold setting (Russell Levers)

  3. "Pop" the carriage

  4. Hold the side lever and pass the carriage in the same direction (all needles in "B")

Slip Stitch is a great way
to add texture and interest to your knitting.
When knitting slip, certain needles do not knit and the working yarn travels UNDER the needles.
When knitting slip, certain needles do not knit and the working yarn travels UNDER needles out of work. Once you understand how slip stitch is created on your machine, the sky's the limit!
  • Slip stitch is most often used as a "wrong-side facing" technique. Floats are left on the purl side of the knitting and the texture is used as the "right" side
  • Slip stitch not only leaves floats on the purl side, it distorts the knitting adding even more texture
  • Combining rows of alternate colors with slip created both texture and color interest (multi-color-slip)
In DesignaKnit use the Slip Stitch symbols Let DAK apply any slip stitch rules for an accurate stitch pattern Send the correct information to the machine to create slip stitch

Because this machine does not have individual slip levers for left and right (unlike other knitting machines), here are 2 work-arounds to create I-cord on your 840.

There are times when you will be picking up stitches in the knitting below the current row. It's helpful to create a marking row for accuracy.
Marker Rows are most easily created with Slip Stitch. With this machine, marker rows are created in a similar way to I-cord.
  1. Carriage on the right
  2. Pull every other needle to "C" or "D" position
  3. Set the Cam lever to S-J
  4. Hold the LEFT Side Lever
  5. Knit Left
  6. The needles in "B" position will not knit, forming small floats as a marker row

3 ways to knit marker rows


NOTE: On this machine, hold the side lever to form slipped stitches over needles in "B" position

The often over-looked technique of Knitweave creates beautiful knitted fabrics with lots of possibilities.
Unlike traditional weaving, think of weaving on the machine as "laying-in" a second yarn on top of the knitting.
It is a decorative technique that can be used to create interesting textures and incorporate yarn that may not be suitable for your machine.
Have a small amount thick, fancy (possibly expensive) yarn? Use it in your machine knitting with Knitweave!


For more about Knit Weave, visit:
the Knit it Now Classroom: Knit Weave

Knit Weave checklist
Weaving brushes engaged (down)
Weaving Stitch pattern (floats not too long)
Cam set to "W"
Carriage on the right
Main yarn in "1" Feeder
Weaving yarn behind LEFT Weaving Yarn Holder
Pull 1st stitch next to carriage to "D"
Knit LEFT
Reverse and repeat

Knit a swatch 60 stitches by 100 rows in Knit Weave

Knit Weave: Notice the floats

Set the cam lever to W
Follow the Interactive Knitting Prompts

Knitting 2 colors in a row with one pass of the carriage is known as Fairisle. When machine knitting place both colors in the yarn feeder of the carriage, let the punchcard instruct the machine to select needles and both colors will knit as instructed.
Tell a hand knitter that you can knit a fairisle hat in an afternoon and they will be amazed.
(PLUS your fairisle will look sooooo much better than hand knitting. )

For more about Fairisle, visit:
the Knit it Now Classroom: Fairisle (Stranded Knitting)
Check out the Knit it Now Stitch Library for Fairisle inspiration!

Fairisle checklist
Set up Interactive Knitting
Weaving brushes not engaged
Russel Levers not engaged (unless partial knitting)
Cam set to "F"
Carriage on the right
Color 1 in "1" Feeder
Color 2 in "2" Feeder
Pull 1st stitch next to carriage to "D"
Continue knitting while pulling 1st needle next to the carriage to "D" EVERY row

Knit a swatch 60 stitches by 100 rows in Fairisle

Fairisle: Notice the Floats

Checklist:
Connect computer, Silverlink, Curl Cord and machine
In Interactive Knitting, set up the swatch size
Set the point cams to the edges of the knitting
Set the cam lever to F
Follow the Interactive Knitting Prompts
Pull the first needle next to the carriage to "D" to control loops at the edges

Often overlooked, Thread Lace is an easy technique to create openwork "lace" fabrics.
It's not fairisle, it's not true lace, but it's a unique stitch pattern that can create beautiful knit fabrics.
Knit with a thick yarn and a very fine yarn, there are lots of possibilities with your machine
NOTE:
Thread lace is knitting is very similar to Fairisle knitting with 2 differences:
  1. Choose a stitch pattern with short floats (1-2 stitches) The yarn is carried behind the "lace" openings. If the floats are too long, the appearance of lace is lost

  2. Don't forget End needle selection: If the edges aren't knitting properly, put 1 end needle to "D" on BOTH SIDES with each pass of the carriage

Punch lace on the 840 is a little different than other stitch patterns on this machine.
It's important to follow each of the steps in your checklist.
Punch Lace Checklist
Cam Lever:L
Russel Levers: (left |) (right ||)
Weaving knobs dis-engaged O"
Carriage on the right Pull end needles to "D"
Main yarn in "1" Feeder
Fine yarn (thread) in @2 feeder (left of the guide pin)
Knit left and end needles DO NOT Knit
Knit Right and end needles knit
Repeat and pull end needles every other row

Knit a swatch 60 stitches by 100 rows in Thread Lace
For success, follow the steps closely, pay attention to end-needle selection and avoid loops at the edges of the knitting.

Punch (Thread) lace: Lace-like "holes" with thread.

Knit 2 strands of yarn together and let the machine position them so you view one color on one side of the knitting and the 2nd color on the other side of the knitting.
This technique is also called Platting or Plating.
This technique can be used on both the single and double bed. It's a great way to bulk up finer yarns and play with color and texture

Knit a swatch 60 stitches by 100 rows in Plating
For success, follow the steps closely, pay attention to how to thread the plating feeder.

Slip Stitch Checklist:
Set the point cams to the edges of the knitting
Thread the plating feeder.
Set the cam lever for stockinette (plain knitting)

Knit transfer-type lace by replacing the regular knitting carriage with the LC-580 Electronic lace carriage.

Don't Skip This

It is critical to understand needle positions when using this lace carriage.
Before operating the carriage MAKE SURE there are no needles in C or D position
Although the Lace Arm is reversible, DO NOT exchange the lace arm with the arm regular carriage or ribber arm.
___________________________
Do not use lace carriage with ribber - drop ribber to the lowest position.

Setting up the lace carriage

  1. Remove the curl cord connector from the regular knitting carriage

  2. Remove the carriage from the needlebed by sliding it all the way to the right

  3. Set it aside in a safe place

  4. With ALL needles in A position Slide the lace carriage onto the needlebed

  5. Pass it back and forth to ensure it's seated correctly

  6. Attach the curl cord

  7. Set the cam lever to "O" (plain knitting)

  8. Pull a few needles to "B" Position and pass the carriage

  9. Push every other needle out of work "A" position.

  10. Set the cam lever to "L"

  11. Pass the carriage slowly and observe the action of the needles

  12. Repeat to get a feel for how the carriage feels when transferring stitches

The machine manual offers a cast on method that makes sense on paper, but in my humble opinion, is not practical.
When using the lace carriage, we cannot pull needles out past the "B" position. Most cast on methods are worked over needles in C or D position, so the manual offers a ravel cord version.
I have 2 objections to this method:
  1. It is difficult to work over more than 40-60 stitches. If you are planning to knit a wider piece, holding down the ravel cord to secure the stitches doesn't work well
  2. It is an open cast on and leaves a sloppy mess along the edge

Suggestions:

1
Use your preferred cast on and knit 2-3 rows with the regular knitting carriage
  • position the lace carriage and continue knitting in lace (remember lace needs even weight for the stitches to form properly (not too much, but even weight)
2
Hang a Cast on Rag
  • Hang a cast on rag
  • Knit 1 row of ravel cord (by hand or with the lace carriage with no patterning)
  • Make sure the needles are in "B" position
  • Knit 1 plain row
  • Continue knitting in lace

The lace carriage comes with cast-on comb type weights, highlighting the importance of having even weight on your work when knitting lace.
A ribber cast on comb is a great solution for having even weight across your work.
If your ribber is attached, notice that the knitting is positioned OVER the ribber
(use cardboard, file folders or magazines to cover the ribber)

Transfers occur in different directions on the same row, requiring multiple passes of the carriage per row.

Plain (Simple) lace
Transfers going in the same direction on each row.

Get comfortable with the Yarn Changer buttons. Without any yarn in the carriage or needles in work, practice and observe the action of the yarn changer.
    2 colors:
  1. Imagine that you've cast on and started knitting with color A
  2. Color B is threaded up in the Yarn Changer
  3. Press Color A button
  4. Manually engage the driving lever
    5. Color A hook is extneded to #2 position
  5. Press the Color B button to position the color B hook in #1 position
